narrative: The model estimated your chance of becoming a bad credit risk at 49.0%, meaning that among applicants with a similar profile, roughly one in two would be expected to run into serious repayment difficulty. At the bank’s approval cut-off, that risk level is too high, so the application was denied. The most influential factor in your assessment was the loan’s purpose: a used car. This factor worked in your favour, and used-car requests are less common among approved applicants. However, the next two most important factors pushed the other way. Your checking-account status of 0–200 DM indicated a low balance and counted against you; only 18.4% of approved applicants fall into this category. The amount you requested, 7,966 DM, was also very high compared with the approved average of about 3,020 DM, which strongly increased the perceived repayment burden. Together, these adverse factors outweighed the favourable purpose signal and kept the overall risk at a level the bank was not prepared to accept. To improve your chances next time, consider requesting a smaller amount, building a stronger checking-account balance, or providing clearer evidence that the repayments are affordable. You could also ask the bank whether a guarantor or co-applicant would help, and seek feedback on what specific evidence would strengthen a future application.
